title: Jensen Huang Is Back at Nvidia. Here's What I'm Doing Now
creator: Couch Investor
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; note: captions garble some names ('Rene Has' for Arm CEO Rene Haas, 'Jensen Wong' for Huang)
summary: Couch Investor (Neil) reacts to Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia president, CEO and board member on Monday morning, after President Trump personally intervened and Arm CEO Rene Haas signed an extension, removing him as a Jensen successor. Nvidia jumped about 31% on the day, with AMD up 6.5%, Micron 19% and Alphabet and Meta about 6.8% each. Neil welcomes the news but warns key-man risk remains: board chair Harvey Jones had said Jensen was not coming back, and he wants a real succession plan and board changes now. He also covers CrowdStrike falling 10.1% on its all-stock acquisition of Zscaler, calling cybersecurity consolidation inevitable as the industry platformizes, and notes neoclouds like IREN (up 22%) and CoreWeave (up about 20%) are still roughly 50% off their peaks, with red daily candles as buyers took profits. The rest is historical context for the sell-off: the Nasdaq-100 fell 10.4% in a week (one in 200 weeks), the S&P 500 is down 12.3% from its 6 October highs, tech's worst week since 2003, the VIX jumped 86% to 35.9, and the S&P now trades around 17x forward earnings versus about 23x late in 2025. He bought Alphabet, Meta, Nvidia, Nebius, Micron and SoFi last week and stays comfortable buying them, though he is not adding right now. Calls: NVDA, GOOGL, META, NBIS, MU, SOFI all BUY reiterated; Alphabet $300-320 possible by year-end.

calls.thesis: BUY reiterated (was BUY 18 Nov). Jensen Huang reinstated as president/CEO/board member Monday morning; NVDA up ~31% on the day. He bought NVDA last week and says if he was comfortable buying last week he is comfortable buying this week - 'Nvidia still not expensive'. Not adding more right now only because he owns enough. Key-man risk remains: no succession plan yet, and he hopes for board changes now Jensen is back.
calls.base_case: The Jensen-exit overhang is removed; funds that sold NVDA purely because Jensen left will be forced to buy back, and shorts must cover after a 20-30% up day.
calls.bull_case: Sentiment shift compounds: a Santa rally into year-end as the whole AI ecosystem re-rates with Jensen back and the fear factor removed.
calls.bear_case: Board/SEC investigation hearings still ahead (next week behind closed doors, more mid-Dec); one green day is not enough data - 'is this sustainable?' is still open; no succession plan if Jensen leaves again.
